summary: ASTRAFIT is an AI-powered astronaut healthcare system developed to support physical health and mental wellbeing during space missions. It integrates AI-assisted ultrasound guidance and image analysis, real-time health monitoring, emergency support, health tracking, and an interactive chatbot with a virtual plant that encourages emotional check-ins. Our working prototype combines a Raspberry Pi 5, MAX30102 heart-rate and SpO₂ sensor, MPU6050 motion sensor, and camera-based ultrasound setup with a software platform that brings these features together. ASTRAFIT addresses the challenges of limited medical access, communication delays, restricted resources, and the psychological effects of isolation during long-duration missions. By combining connected hardware, AI assistance, and wellbeing support, our goal is to help astronauts monitor their health, access guidance, and maintain wellbeing when immediate support from Earth is unavailable. Ultimately, ASTRAFIT aims to make healthcare more accessible beyond Earth and contribute to safer, healthier space exploration.
details:
ASTRAFIT – Project Details

What does it do and how does it work?

ASTRAFIT is an integrated AI-powered astronaut healthcare system designed to support physical health and mental wellbeing during space missions. It combines AI-assisted ultrasound guidance and image analysis, vital-sign monitoring, emergency support, health tracking, and an interactive chatbot with a virtual plant that encourages emotional check-ins.

The system connects hardware sensors to a central software platform. The MAX30102 monitors heart rate and blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂), while the MPU6050 tracks movement and orientation. Astronauts can also access ultrasound guidance and image analysis to support medical assessments, alongside wellbeing features through the application.

What benefits does it have?

ASTRAFIT brings multiple healthcare and wellbeing features into one platform. It aims to improve health awareness, make medical guidance more accessible, support ultrasound procedures, and encourage astronauts to maintain their emotional wellbeing. Having these tools together can be particularly valuable when immediate medical assistance from Earth is limited.

What is the intended impact?

Our goal is to contribute to safer and healthier long-duration space missions by supporting astronauts both physically and mentally. ASTRAFIT aims to reduce dependence on immediate Earth-based assistance, encourage earlier awareness of health changes, and provide accessible support in isolated environments.

What tools, languages, hardware, and software did we use?

  • Programming: Python, TypeScript, JavaScript, HTML and CSS.
  • Frontend: React and TypeScript.
  • Hardware: Raspberry Pi 5, MAX30102 heart-rate and SpO₂ sensor, MPU6050 motion sensor, and a camera-based ultrasound guidance setup.
  • Software and technologies: Python sensor integration, AI-assisted image analysis, computer vision, and a web-based dashboard.
  • Research: NASA's publicly available research and Open Science Data Repository resources to understand astronaut health and spaceflight challenges.

How is the project creative?

ASTRAFIT combines medical assistance, connected hardware, AI-supported ultrasound, and emotional wellbeing in one astronaut-focused platform. Its interactive chatbot and virtual plant introduce an engaging way to encourage daily emotional check-ins, making wellbeing part of the overall healthcare experience rather than treating it as a separate concern.

What factors did our team consider?

We considered the unique conditions of space missions, including isolation, communication delays, limited medical equipment, restricted resources, and the difficulty of accessing medical specialists. We also considered the importance of an accessible interface, reliable sensor integration, and supporting both physical and mental wellbeing during long-duration missions.
